# A query-first radial-blur invariant for particle-motion currents

Private constructive investigation, 29 October 2026. This is a conditional
mathematical acquisition operation. No torque measurement, new optical access,
historical novelty or practical advantage is claimed. The public-data consumer
and its source qualifications are separate from the theorem.

## 1. Question and strongest ordinary starting point

Can one acquire a mechanically meaningful quadratic motion query directly from
raw particle images, without first estimating a velocity field, a particle-image
diameter, or the full displacement distribution? Pressure-free force identities,
virtual-work fields, single-pixel PIV/Reynolds-stress inference and holomorphic
blur-invariant moments already exist. They are the ordinary starting point, not
results invented here. The construction below combines their query-first
viewpoints and discriminates which virtual loads are compatible with exact
radial-blur invariance.

The native output is a finite-lag displacement current. Converting it to a
hydrodynamic torque requires the additional conditions in section 7. The
translational-force counterpart fails within the stated harmonic-field package.

## 2. Classification of the blur-compatible quadratic query

Identify R^2 with C. Let S(x) be a C^2 real symmetric 2-by-2 matrix on a domain
not containing its singularities, and put

    f(x,y) = (y-x)^T S(x) (y-x).

For every x,y in an open product domain, invariance under every sufficiently
small radial probability perturbation of x and y, independently, holds if and
only if f is harmonic separately in x and y. Necessity follows by using uniform
probability on circles of radius t and the expansion

    average_circle f = f + t^2 Delta f/4 + o(t^2).

Sufficiency is the harmonic mean-value theorem, followed by integrating over
the radial distribution of the perturbation. It requires the entire supporting
disk to lie in a harmonic neighborhood. It is not a statement about arbitrary
unknown support or about kernels crossing a pole.

Writing D=y-x gives the literal identities

    Delta_y f = 2 tr S,
    Delta_x f = D^T (Delta S) D - 4 (div S) . D + 2 tr S.

Since D ranges over an open set, separate harmonicity is equivalent to

    tr S = 0,       div S = 0,       Delta S = 0.                 (2.1)

# A difference-image control variate, and what it actually repairs

This supplements PROOF.md. Generic image differencing and image structure
functions are established methods, notably Cerbino--Trappe, PRL100,188102
(2008), DOI10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.188102. This is a query-specific composition
with holomorphic moments, not a new claim to differential dynamic microscopy.

## 1. Exact zero controls

Write Q(I,J) for the population bilinear harmonic covariance functional in
PROOF.md (5.2). In the full-aperture Poisson/radial model,

    Q(I0,I0)=Q(I1,I1)=0.                                      (D1)

This extension requires BOTH endpoint blur disks to avoid the pole. The
forward-only theorem allowed an endpoint PSF with merely finite second
moment; that weaker contract does not suffice for the Laurent weights now
also used on the endpoint image.

Indeed the single-particle contribution is the same separate-PSF average of
K(x+xi,x+eta); its value is K(x,x)=0. Within one image the mixed brightness
moment is E B_j^2 rather than E B0 B1, but it multiplies zero. The two PSF
integrations are independent integration variables even when the PSF profile
is the same. A pixel-diagonal photon or independent-pixel electronics
covariance also vanishes because K(z,z)=0. General spatially correlated
electronics do NOT vanish automatically. Quantized weights leave the explicit
finite arithmetic errors in the consumer.

Consequently

    -Q(I1-I0,I1-I0)/2
      = [Q(I0,I1)+Q(I1,I0)]/2                               (D2)

in expectation. This acquires the symmetrized finite-lag current

    Fsym = E [K(x,y)+K(y,x)]/2.

It is not exactly the forward finite-lag current. If speed <=U, material
acceleration <=A, ||S||<=Smax and the spatial Lipschitz constant of S is LS on
the particle segments, then its difference from the start-time quadratic
current after division by delta^2 is at most

    Smax [U A delta + A^2 delta^2/4] + LS U^3 delta/2.

This follows by PROOF.md (7.2) for the forward term and by

annular tensor, Smax<=|beta|/amin^2 and LS<=2|beta|/amin^3 when all segments
stay at radius >=amin. No time-reversal symmetry of the flow is used.

# Result: a conditional raw-image current operation, with an honest source failure

The substantive construction is a query-specific radial-blur invariant,
not a physically qualified torque measurement. It identifies exactly which
quadratic virtual-field queries survive radial blur, derives the rotational
annular query, supplies a difference-image control that removes static
unmatched-particle variance, and executes the finite-bit operation on all500
frames of a real public particle-image record. That record fails the
positive-normalizer gate. No physical or practical advantage is established.

## Acquired mathematical operation

For f(x,y)=(y-x)^T S(x)(y-x), invariance under every sufficiently small radial
blur in both variables is equivalent to trS=divS=DeltaS=0. A solenoidal
virtual field therefore needs to be harmonic as well. On an annulus,
w=(alpha+beta/r^2)Jx realizes a unit inner rotation and zero outer rotation;
the translational full-Dirichlet counterpart is incompatible. The resulting
finite-lag current kernel is

    K(z,zeta)=-beta Im[zeta^2/z^2-2zeta/z].

Two complex bilinear correlations implement it: four real covariances plus
one real normalization covariance. Support disks avoiding the Laurent pole,
full aperture or calibrated tails, linear imaging and the positive connected
particle-pair law are necessary inputs. Arbitrary unknown PSF support is not
covered. PROOF.md gives finite-aperture, integrated-pixel, boundary-strip and
finite-lag obligations rather than granting them.

The simpler full-image covariance has a real statistical cost: for a static
uniform cloud in1<r<2, even with exact means and particle-count normalization,
its variance is [160ln2/27-26/9]/n>1.2/n, independent of particle count.
Subtracting same-frame zero-expectation harmonic controls yields the exact
symmetric current -Q(I1-I0,I1-I0)/2. Under a fixed Poisson matched-pair law,
common per-particle brightness and no camera/photon noise its variance is
O(displacement^4/n), so division by
lag^2 does not incur that particular lag^-4 variance penalty. DDM already
supplies generic image differencing; this is an explicit query specialization.
Different endpoint PSF profiles remain allowed, but BOTH blur disks now must
avoid the pole. Gain mismatch and detector noise can restore a variance floor.
